question: To determine the average number of children living in single-family homes, a researcher picks a simple random sample of 50 such homes. However, even after one follow-up visit the interviewer is unable to make contact with anyone in 8 of these homes. Concerned about nonresponse bias, the researcher picks another simple random sample and instructs the interviewer to keep trying until contact is made with someone in a total of 50 homes. The average number of children is determined to be 1.73. Is this estimate probably too low or too high?

options.0: Too high, because of undercoverage bias.
options.1: Too low, because convenience samples overestimate average results.
options.2: Too low, because of undercoverage bias.
options.3: Too high, because convenience samples overestimate average results.

question: The principal of a school is interested in estimating the average income per family of her students. She selects a random sample of students and collects information about their family income. A 95 percent confidence interval computed from this data for the mean income per family is ($35,095, $45,005). Which of the following provides the best interpretation of this confidence interval?

options.0: There is a 95% probability that the mean income per family in the school is between $35,095 and $45,005.
options.1: There is a 95% probability that the families of all the students in this school have an income of between $35,095 and $45,005.
options.2: 95 percent of the students in her school are from families whose income is between $35,095 and $45,005.
options.3: If we were to take another sample of the same size and compute a 95 percent confidence interval, we would have a 95% chance of getting the interval ($35,095, $45,005).

question: A survey was conducted to determine the percentage of parents who would support raising the legal driving age to 18. The results were stated as 67% with a margin of error of ±3%. What is meant by ±3%?

options.0: It is unlikely that the given sample proportion result could be obtained unless the true percentage was between 64% and 70%.
options.1: The percentage of the entire population of parents who would support raising the driving age is between 64% and 70%.
options.2: Three percent of the population were not surveyed.
options.3: In the sample, the percentage of parents who would support raising the driving age is between 64% and 70%.

A 12-ounce soft drink has 41 grams of sugar, which is 14% of the normal daily allowance for sugar. Approximately how many grams of sugar are recommended in the normal diet?

Fifty oranges of one variety were selected at random and weighed. A 95 percent confidence interval computed from the sample weights to estimate the mean weight of oranges of this variety is (7.58, 8.72) ounces. Which of the following statements is true with respect to the confidence level used?

options.0: In repeated samplings of the same size, 95 percent of the intervals constructed will contain the sampled mean weight of the oranges.
options.1: In repeated samplings of the same size, 95 percent of the intervals constructed will contain the true mean weight of the oranges of this variety.
options.2: Ninety-five percent of the oranges in this sample weigh between 7.58 and 8.72 ounces.
options.3: Ninety-five percent of the oranges of this variety weigh between 7.58 and 8.72 ounces.

II. If every continuous real-valued function defined on K is bounded, then K is compact.
III. If K is compact, then K is connected.
